headline: New law places about 173 acres in San Diego County into federal trust for the Jamul Indian Village and bans gaming there.
what_it_does: The law takes about 172 acres of specified land in San Diego County, California, into trust for the Jamul Indian Village of California, making it part of the tribe's reservation. It also requires the Department of the Interior to accept and hold in trust another 1.1 acres once the tribe transfers that land to the United States. Gaming is not allowed on any of the land taken into trust.

who_it_affects.group: Members of the Jamul Indian Village of California
who_it_affects.how: Their tribe's reservation grows by about 172 acres, with another 1.1 acres to be added once the tribe transfers it to the United States.
It must accept title to the additional 1.1 acres and hold it in trust for the tribe once that land is transferred.
They may not run gaming on any of the land placed into trust under this law.

when_it_takes_effect: The 172 acres are taken into trust when the law was enacted on December 23, 2024; the extra 1.1 acres are added once the tribe transfers that land to the United States.
